**Goal:** Build a github repo and create an app with the name AI Stock Bot that will be a project that trains an AI to buy and sell stocks in a sandbox with the intention of using it in the real world. - `walkforward.py` — one agent per test year, stitched out-of-sample track record, criteria check
- `live/` — `SimulatedBroker` (persistent JSON paper account), `AlpacaBroker` (Alpaca paper REST API), `run_paper_day`, `latest_signal`
- CLI: `download | run | walkforward | compare | backtest | signal | paper`

## Decisions (made autonomously)
- **"Makes money" definition** (`evaluation/criteria.py`): on a fully out-of-sample walk-forward track record, after costs (5 bp commission + 5 bp slippage per trade): total return > 0, CAGR >= 5%, Sharpe >= 0.6, max drawdown >= -30%, profitable in >= 60% of test years. Beating buy-and-hold is reported but not required (it is a risk-reduction strategy; B&H in a bull market is a very high bar).
- Agent is a market-timing agent per symbol (exposure 0 / 50 / 100%), equal-weight sleeves across a 20-symbol universe. Trained on all symbols jointly (scale-free features) so the policy generalises.
- Env no longer re-trades to the same target every day (was causing ~10k tiny trades); position drifts until the decision changes.
- Real-world bridge: Alpaca paper trading (free, keys via `ALPACA_API_KEY_ID` / `ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY`) — cannot be exercised here without keys, so tested with a fake HTTP session. `SimulatedBroker` allows forward testing without any account.
- Sandbox "application" = Python + gymnasium + stable-baselines3 + yfinance (all pip-installed); no external trading app needed.

## Experiment log (test = 2023-01-01 .. 2026-10, equal-weight 20 symbols)
| run | test return | Sharpe | MaxDD | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp01_baseline | +32.7% | 0.82 | -15.5% | raw log-return reward |
| exp02_scaled | +44.6% | 1.01 | -14.7% | reward x100, turnover penalty |
| exp03_excess | +71.8% | 1.37 | -11.6% | + reward relative to buy&hold |
| buy_and_hold | +132.0% | 1.61 | -18.6% | benchmark |
| trend_sma200 | +68.5% | 1.29 | -14.3% | benchmark |

## Walk-forward results (2015-2026, each year unseen, costs included)
| run | total | CAGR | Sharpe | MaxDD | years profitable | criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wf_excess_weekly | +170.8% | +8.8% | 0.83 | -23.1% | 11/12 | PASS |
| wf_weekly_mkt | +145.5% | +7.9% | 0.72 | -21.2% | 8/12 | PASS |
| wf_biweekly | +128.1% | +7.3% | 0.64 | -21.0% | 10/12 | PASS |
| wf_excess_daily | +100.0% | +6.1% | 0.60 | -19.5% | 9/12 | FAIL (Sharpe 0.598) |
| buy_and_hold | +507.5% | +16.6% | 0.98 | -32.2% | | |
| trend_sma200 | +230.0% | +10.7% | 1.02 | -14.3% | | |

- Weekly decisions (decision_interval=5) beat daily decisions; adding SPY market context and moving to biweekly decisions did not help further. I stopped iterating after two rounds to limit selection bias on the walk-forward period.
- Deployable model: `runs/wf_excess_weekly/fold_2026` (trained < 2024, validated 2024-2025, +16.8% on 2026 YTD). Run artifacts in `runs/` are gitignored, so regenerate them with `python -m ai_stock_bot walkforward --config configs/wf_excess_weekly.json --jobs 3` (~45 min on 6 CPUs).
- Paper trading smoke-tested on live Yahoo data (2026-11-04): `python -m ai_stock_bot paper runs/wf_excess_weekly/fold_2026 --refresh`.
- Known limitations: the agent underperforms buy-and-hold on total return (~57% average exposure) and does not beat the SMA-200 trend filter on Sharpe. The universe is chosen with hindsight (today's large caps), which is a survivorship bias. The Alpaca adapter is untested against the live API because no keys are available.

## Possible next steps
- Forward-test daily with `paper` for several months before using real money.
- Point-in-time universe to remove survivorship bias; cross-sectional (portfolio-weight) action space; more seeds.

## Stage 4: robustness (`robustness.py`, CLI `robustness`)
Re-trades the saved walk-forward agents (no retraining) through:
- real history (sanity check; reproduces the walk-forward exactly, which a test asserts);
- 2x/3x costs;
- start-day offsets 1-4;
- unseen symbols (VERSATILITY set of 16, incl. TLT/GLD/EFA);
- 20 block-bootstrap alternate histories;
- 10 day-shuffled pattern-free histories (leakage check).

Also reported: seed spread, and a final HOLDOUT set of 10 symbols that is looked at once, for the final model only.

Findings on wf_excess_weekly (first suite run):
- Profitable in every scenario.
- Sharpe depends on the trading weekday (0.54-0.83), so the headline 0.83 was partly luck.
- Timing edge on real history is -0.9%/yr: the bot does NOT beat holding its average exposure constantly. Its profit comes from partial exposure to a rising market, not from timing skill. This is now a required check (`timing edge on real history > 0`).
- Bug found and fixed: the bootstrap resampled each symbol independently, destroying cross-correlation (B&H Sharpe 3.0). It now uses common blocks across symbols.
- The shuffled-edge check is now one-sided (positive = leakage).

Variants trained to look for real skill (walk-forward Sharpe; constant-50% benchmark = 1.01, B&H = 0.98):
- wf_w_wide (+20 train-only symbols): 1.01
- wf_excess_weekly: 0.83
- wf_w_5seeds: 0.77
- wf_w_risk (variance penalty): 0.68
- wf_w_wider (+67 train-only): 0.67
- wf_w_bench50 (reward vs 50%): 0.61
- wf_w_wide_aug: 0.60

- No consistent winner: differences between variants are mostly training noise.
- wf_mega, a 22-model ensemble of all weekly-family runs per fold (`ensemble` CLI), scores Sharpe 0.76 vs constant-50% 1.01. Averaged over the noise, PPO timing has no skill on this universe.
- Smoothed daily decisions (`SmoothedPolicy`, `robustness --smooth 5`) remove the weekday lottery: wide Sharpe across start days goes from 0.40-1.01 to 0.84-0.89, bootstrap median Sharpe from 0.70 to 0.91. Adopted for deployment. Timing edge is still about -1.4%/yr.
- The skill check now averages the edge over the 5 start days.

- wf_w_compact (window 1, net 32x32): 0.72; smoothed robustness about the same as wide.
- wf_w_xs (cross-sectional rank features): 0.73.

Diagnosis (scratchpad probes, not committed):
- In-sample, i.e. on its own training data, the trained agent ALSO trails a static 50% position: Sharpe 0.40-0.7
